title: Predicate and Quantifier Logic
purpose: Seed first-order predicate/quantifier reasoning over bounded Lantern domains so variables, all/some/none and existential claims need not be rediscovered experientially.

concepts.definition: An expression that becomes a proposition when its argument positions are bound to terms.
A constant, entity reference, or variable that may occupy an argument position.
A term referring to a particular object within the interpretation.
A placeholder whose value is supplied by a binding within a declared domain.
An assignment of a permitted term/entity to a variable for evaluating a formula or applying a rule.
The number of argument positions a predicate takes.
FOR ALL x in domain D, formula P(x) holds.
THERE EXISTS at least one x in domain D for which P(x) holds.
The subformula governed by a quantifier; changing scope can change meaning.
A variable occurrence not bound by a quantifier or local rule binding.
A variable occurrence governed by a quantifier or explicit rule binding.
A particular binding that satisfies an existential claim.
A permitted binding for which a universally quantified claim fails.
The explicitly bounded set/type of candidate values over which a quantifier ranges.

guards.reason: A universal statement alone does not establish that the domain contains a P-object.
One or more witnesses do not establish a universal.
An existential claim does not identify a particular witness unless evidence binds it.
Each x may have a different y; quantifier order changes meaning.
This transformation can be misleading without explicit domain/existence conditions and must not be performed as a generic scope rewrite.
A conclusion may not introduce an unbound variable with no rule binding.
Quantified claims do not silently transfer between domains/scopes.
Existential support is not universal support.

invariants: Every quantifier has an explicit or recoverable domain/scope.
Existential claims require at least one witness but do not identify a witness unless bound.
All does not imply existence unless existence/domain nonemptiness is separately established.
Some means at least one, not most and not all.
No means universal negation within the stated domain.
Free variables may not enter authoritative or candidate conclusions accidentally.
Bindings preserve argument roles; swapping predicate arguments is not licensed by quantification.
Formal derivability remains separate from empirical truth and authority.

provenance.authoring_basis: Standard first-order predicate and quantifier logic, constrained for bounded inspectable Lantern inference.
